description: Say whether a crawler may fetch a path under a robots.txt file, by the rules of RFC 9309 (Robots Exclusion Protocol, September 2022). Send the robots.txt text you already have (up to 20,000 characters), the crawler's product token (for example Googlebot or GPTBot) and the path with its query (for example /private/page?x=1). Get back allowed or disallowed, the rule that decided it with its line number, which user-agent group was used (the crawler's own group or the * group), every rule that matched, and each line the protocol does not accept, with its line number. Nothing is fetched: you send the text. Answer fields: ok, verdict, result, rule, does_not, sources, observation, signature, verify. Errors: ok false with the reason (bad input, too large, hourly limit). Free. No model, no network, nothing you send is stored by the tool, and every answer is signed with LLPRO's key (check it at https://llpro.ai/robots-txt-check). Not legal, tax or financial advice.

path.description: The path and query of the URL to check, starting with / (e.g. /docs/a.pdf?v=2). Not the full URL; leave out the #fragment.

robots_txt.description: The robots.txt file text exactly as served (line breaks CRLF, LF or CR), up to 20,000 characters. An empty text means no rules.

user_agent.description: The crawler's product token, e.g. Googlebot, GPTBot, ClaudeBot, bingbot (letters, _ and -; matched without regard to case).

name: robots_txt_check
title: robots.txt Rule Check (RFC 9309)
